name: PadCare Labs
tagline: Collection and recycling of used sanitary pads
excerpt: PadCare Labs, which collects and recycles used sanitary pads, drew a rush of offers on Shark Tank India Season 2 and raised ₹1 crore.
content:
PadCare Labs installs bins that collect used sanitary pads in offices, factories and housing societies, and recycles the waste into reusable materials instead of sending it to landfill or incinerators. It was founded by Ajinkya Dhariya.

Dhariya pitched in Shark Tank India Season 2, Episode 23. The sharks competed to invest, and YourStory reported that the company raised ₹1 crore on the show. Inc42 later listed PadCare Labs among the 2023 investments of Namita Thapar and Vineeta Singh.

Since then the company has raised institutional money. Inc42 and Entrackr reported in February 2026 a pre-Series A round of ₹27.2 crore (about $3 million), a mix of equity and debt led by Zerodha's Rainmatter, with 3one4 Capital and Brigade REAP among the new investors. Revenue and valuation have not been reported in the outlets we track.

PadCare shows how a hygiene problem that is rarely discussed can become a fundable business when it serves companies' waste and sustainability obligations.

faq.q: Did PadCare get a deal on Shark Tank India?
faq.a: Yes. YourStory reported that it raised ₹1 crore on Season 2, Episode 23.

faq.q: Has PadCare raised money since the show?
faq.a: Yes. It raised ₹27.2 crore in a pre-Series A round led by Rainmatter, reported in February 2026.
It has not been publicly disclosed in the reports we track.

lessons: Selling to institutions (offices, factories, housing societies) can give a social-impact product a reliable revenue model.
A pitch that solves a widely felt but rarely discussed problem can trigger competition among investors.
Climate and impact investors became the natural next round after the show.
